title: Or with a friend
hook: in the middle of the rhinoceros poem, a door opens: if you find a wise companion, walk with them
carry: we praise the blessing of companionship

segments.voice: Yesterday: khaggavisana, the one horn, and your line, alone like the rhinoceros. Today the same poem turns a corner.

Verse after verse, the rhinoceros poem ends the same way: wander alone. Read it fast and you'd think the whole message is: don't need anyone. But look near the start. Two verses sit side by side, and they don't end the way the others do. They start with the word if. If you find someone. It's like a long letter from a friend who keeps saying I'm fine on my own, I'm fine on my own, and then, partway down the page, writes: unless you'd like to come.
screen: `VERSE AFTER VERSE: WANDER ALONE.` → `THEN, EARLY ON: IF.` → `UNLESS YOU'D LIKE TO COME.`

segments.voice: Roughly, the verse says: if you find a wise companion, a fellow traveler who lives well and is steady, walk with them, overcoming every danger, glad and mindful. And the next: if you don't find one like that, walk alone, like a king who has left a conquered kingdom behind, like an elephant alone in the forest. So solitude was never the goal. It's what you do when the right companion isn't there. The poem even says what makes a companion right. Wise: the Pali word is nipaka, skilled, discerning. Living well. Steady. Someone who makes the dangers smaller, not bigger. A little later comes a line like a proverb: we praise the blessing of companionship. Keep company with those better than you or equal to you. If you can't find them, live blamelessly and walk alone. Elsewhere in the discourses, Ananda, the Buddha's attendant, says: good friendship is half of the spiritual life. And the Buddha corrects him: don't say that, Ananda. Good friendship is the whole of the spiritual life. So the tradition holds both, the one horn and the good friend. Not a contradiction: two pictures of the same freedom. You don't need a crowd. And when someone wise and kind turns up on your road, you don't need to walk alone either.
screen: `IF YOU FIND A WISE COMPANION` · `IF NOT, WALK ALONE` · `WISE, STEADY, LIVING WELL` · `FRIENDSHIP IS THE WHOLE OF IT` · then, large: `OR WITH A FRIEND.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who makes the road safer, wise, steady and kind, near or far or no longer living, and picture walking beside them, matching steps, not talking much. If there's no one like that right now, picture the friend you'd like to find, and the friend you'd like to be, and rest in that company.
sahaya. The turn in the rhinoceros poem: if you find a wise and steady companion, walk with them, glad and mindful. Today's word.
Your line: we praise the blessing of companionship. The one horn and the good friend, both. Day five hundred eighty, done.

howItsDone: Buddhist teaching speaks of the kalyanamitta, the good or noble friend, and Buddhists practice in groups, with a teacher, or with a trusted companion, alongside times of solitude.

fork.setup: you're Ananda. you've been thinking about friendship and say: good friends are half of the spiritual life. what does the Buddha say?
options: don't say that: it's the whole of it.
fork.reveal: in the discourse called Half, the Buddha tells Ananda that good friendship is the whole of the spiritual life.

original.note: Pali sahaya: companion, friend. the rhinoceros poem's wise companion is a nipaka sahaya.

trapdoor: what you thought: the rhinoceros poem is all about being alone.
what it means: solitude is what you do when no wise companion is there; when one is, you walk together.
what a scholar hears: Sn 45–46 set the companion verse beside the solitary refrain, and SN 45.2 calls good friendship the whole of the holy life.

chat.says: Didn't the rhinoceros poem say walk alone? So no friends at all?
options: Only if no wise companion turns up; if one does, walk together, glad.
Right: it says any friend will slow a seeker down on the path.
Friends are fine, as long as they agree with everything you think.
chat.meaning: The poem says: if you find a wise, steady companion, walk with them; if not, walk alone. The Buddha calls good friendship the whole of the spiritual life.
